[NLFC.2.5] **The engine reports its next deadline.**
`ds_engine_next_deadline_ns` must report the earliest deadline later than the
monotonic clock's current value ([LTIM.2.8.2]), or that the engine holds none. A
deadline is one of these instants, whether or not a rule acts on it:

- the `fire_at` of a live timer fact ([LTAC.3.2], [LCCO.7.2]);
- the expiry of a live fact that has a TTL ([LDTL.1.1]);
- the expiry of a cache entry ([NSTG.2.4.2]).

The call is a read, on a live or a mock clock. It must not take a clock sample
([NTST.3.3]), must record nothing, and must not change what any later call or
pump does. Two conforming engines given the same program, inputs and clock
values must report the same answer. A NULL argument is `DS_ERR_INVAL`, and a call
from inside a callback is refused as [RARC.13.16] states.

An instant at which a time-dependent condition changes ([LTIM.2.4.1]) is not a
deadline, and neither is the end of a cooldown ([LCDB.3.2.1]). A host that
depends on such a condition pumps on a cadence of its own.

The integrator may call this or not, and may pump on any cadence
([NADP.1.1]). The engine does nothing at a deadline until a pump
([LCCO.7.2], [NSTG.2.4.2]).
